subject: APAC edge + EU fallback: capacity & timeline for AQ-2027-117
messages:
From: Sana Gupta <sana@aquila.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@aquila.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity ask: APAC edge pool + EU fallback for AQ-2027-117

Irene / Karthik —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Aquila is moving quickly on a pilot that will be latency-sensitive across Singapore and Sydney with a secondary EU failover for compliance & data residency. High level ask: we need a dedicated pool sizing recommendation and delivery timeline for an initial 6-month pilot tied to deal AQ-2027-117.

Key pointers from our side:
- Expected burst QPS: 220 peak concurrent inference sessions (short chat style requests, avg 120 tokens)
- Sustained baseline: ~45 QPS across APAC region
- EU fallback only for <5% of traffic during regional outage or for EU-resident users
- Compliance: SOC2 + Data residency in EU required for subsets of logs

Questions: what GPU types do you recommend (cost vs latency), lead times for an APAC edge micro-pool (Singapore) and an EU fallback node, and can we include an SLA lane for pilot? Also please send the SOW + any sizing workbook we can review.

Can you get back with a straw-man by EOD Friday our time? We are hoping to sign SOW in the next two weeks.

— Sana
Sana Gupta
Head of Platform Integrations, Aquila AI
[Attachment: Aquila_MAL_plan_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Gupta <sana@aquila.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 13:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity ask: APAC edge pool + EU fallback for AQ-2027-117

Sana —

Thanks for the clear summary and the workbook. I’ve looped in Karthik and Ben from capacity planning and Monica on procurement/terms. Quick responses below; we’ll produce a short straw-man sizing + timeline and follow up with a proposed SOW.

Initial thoughts:
- GPU choices: A100->lowest-latency option; H100 offers better perf/price on large-context workloads but depends on model size. For chat with avg 120 tokens A100 in 16GB mixed-precision config looks safe for predictable latency; if Aquila wants to optimize unit cost we can run a perf estimate for H100 and quantized M60/X variants.
- APAC micro-pool (Singapore): for 220 peak concurrent short sessions we estimate needing ~10 dedicated x A100 (conservative), with autoscale burst to additional shared nodes. That maps to ~40-60 RU (reserved units) depending on model (we’ll send the RU->GPU mapping).
- EU fallback node: a small standby pool (2-3 A100 equivalents) that can be woken up or accept <=5% traffic.
- Lead times: standby/incremental allocation in hosted zones: 10–14 business days once SOW and PO are in place; full dedicated capacity provisioning on Reserved hardware (if required on customer-only rack) can be 6–8 weeks.

Action items I’m assigning to Karthik / Ben to firm up numbers + attach sizing workbook back to Sana. Monica — please start a draft SOW (procurement-friendly with a clear pilot SLA lane).

Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Architecture — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sana Gupta <sana@aquila.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity ask: APAC edge pool + EU fallback for AQ-2027-117

Irene / team / Sana —

I pulled a quick workload model from the attached Aquila_MAL_plan_v2.xlsx and made a couple of assumptions (listed in the workbook tab "assumptions"): model = open-chat-70B-like; avg latency target (p95) = 220ms; request shape = median 120 tokens in/out.

Sizing summary (straw-man):
- APAC (Singapore) dedicated pool: 10 x A100 (single-slot) + structured autoscale to 4 shared H100s for burst. Estimated RU mapping = 48 reserved units -> expected steady cost band.
- EU fallback: 3 x A100-equivalent (can be NVMe-backed nodes to speed cold start for KV cache); set up with policy to accept only EU-resident traffic or failover routing.
- Network and KV cache considerations: recommend colocating KV cache in APAC edge to keep tail latency low; cross-region replication for EU fallback (async) to limit bandwidth.
- Cost/lead time notes: provisional pricing in workbook (tab "costs"); procurement lead = Monica, but if Aquila needs hardware-reserved racks add 4–6 weeks.

Attached draft workbook has a simple RU->GPU mapping and a short runbook for failover. I flagged two risk items: 1) model growth beyond 70B equivalent changes RU needs by ~25%, 2) EU logging/residency requires a specific audit path that affects retention costs.

[Attachment: Aquila_MAL_plan_v2.xlsx (updated) — see tab "strat-sizing-v1"]

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Technical Program Manager, Capacity — Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Gupta <sana@aquila.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@aquila.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity ask: APAC edge pool + EU fallback for AQ-2027-117 — proposed SOW + next steps

Sana / Tom —

Appreciate the quick turn. Attached is a short SOW draft (SOW_Aquila_Draft_1.pdf) and the sizing workbook that Karthik updated. High level proposal:

1) Pilot scope (6 months): 10 x A100 dedicated in Singapore (reserved), EU fallback 3-node standby; autoscale policy to burst to shared H100s up to +40% capacity.
2) SLA lane: p95 < 300ms for APAC-resident users under pilot traffic (detailed in SOW appendix).
3) Compliance: we will keep EU logs in EU retention buckets; redact PII on ingest (we will deliver SOC2 artifact set during procurement).
4) Delivery: targeted activation of APAC micro-pool within 10 business days after signed SOW + PO; full reserved hardware available in 6 weeks if Aquila opts for dedicated racks.

Next steps:
- Monica will send a procurement-friendly SOW with payment terms for your legal team (cc’d).
- Can we set a 30-minute sync Monday (your morning) to walk the SOW and finalize the pilot SLA? Proposed slots: Mon 15 Mar 09:00 or 11:00 SGT.

Thanks — we’ll keep the EU fallback policy conservative until we confirm residency audiences.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Architecture
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOW_Aquila_Draft_1.pdf (pdf)]
